Definition: perhaps akin to the base of G3022 (from the whitish hair); a wolf:--wolf.
BiblicalUsage: The word means a wolf, and Jesus uses it for the false prophets who come in sheep's clothing but inwardly are ravening wolves, and for the danger His disciples face, sent as lambs among wolves. The hireling sees the wolf coming and flees, because the sheep are not his own, and Paul warns the Ephesian elders that after his departing grievous wolves will enter in among them, not sparing the flock.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the wolf is Scripture's plainest picture of false teaching: it looks like a sheep until it is close enough to kill. I hold that the true Shepherd does not flee when the wolf comes, and the test of any shepherd is whether he stays with the flock when it costs him.
